title: The Magnetic Field Acting upon Nuclei in Molecules is Shielded
lead: Inside a molecule a nucleus sits among electrons whose own magnetic field changes the field the nucleus feels from the magnet.
notes: The book's page carries no author credit.
exercise_notes: The one exercise was written by AI with an AI solution; its Bloom level and concept tags were chosen by AI.

exercises.source_id: If the magnetic field experienced by the nucleus is lower than the external magnetic field
exercises.prompt: A molecule is placed in an external magnetic field $\kBx = 7.050000$ T. One of its nuclei experiences a field $\kBy = 7.049820$ T. Is that nucleus shielded or deshielded?

answer.hint: Compare the field the nucleus experiences with the external field.
answer.solution: The field the nucleus experiences is lower than the external field, $\kBy < \kBx$ (by 0.000180 T), so the nucleus is shielded.

footnotes.html: The nucleus does experience the external field, but changed by the field of the surrounding electrons, as the rest of the sentence says; it is the external field alone that it does not feel.
